title: Local-tooling scaffolders (hooks install, ci scaffold) are idempotent and deny-by-default
statement: devai adopt hooks install MUST be idempotent: re-running against an already-installed hook file MUST update the marker-delimited block in place rather than duplicating it, and MUST preserve any surrounding hook content (e.g. lint-staged invocations) untouched. devai adopt ci scaffold MUST be deny-by-default: with --write and no --force, an existing file at the target path MUST NOT be overwritten. Both verbs MUST be plan-only (no filesystem writes) unless --write is passed.
rationale: Both verbs write into artifacts a human or another tool may already be maintaining (a git hook file, a CI workflow file). Per Article 36 and the D-99 per-batch verification discipline, a scaffolder that silently duplicates content on re-run or silently clobbers an adopter's hand-edited CI workflow would corrupt exactly the local tooling it exists to help set up — the plan/--write split and the deny-by-default/idempotent-update guarantees are what make repeated invocation safe.

strategy.rationale: The registered test corpus provides deterministic regression evidence for this invariant.
